title.zh: 卷六十四 志第四十 儀衞
title.raw: 卷六十四 志第四十 儀衞 Volume 64 Treatises 40: Ceremonial Guards

sentences.zh: 卷六十四 志第四十

translations.literal: Volume 64, Treatise 40
translations.idiomatic: Volume 64, Treatise 40

sentences.zh: ◎儀衛 《周官》，王之儀衛分掌於天官、春官、夏官之屬，而蹕事則專屬於秋官。

translations.literal: ◎ Ceremonial Guards. In the Offices of Zhou, the king's ceremonial guards and escorts were divided among the subordinate offices of Heaven, Spring, and Summer, while road-clearing duties belonged exclusively to the Autumn Office.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Ceremonial Guards. Under the Offices of Zhou, the sovereign's ceremonial escort was apportioned among the bureaus of Heaven, Spring, and Summer; clearing the imperial way fell solely to the Autumn Office.

sentences.zh: 漢朝會，則衛官陳車騎，張旗幟。

translations.literal: At Han imperial assemblies, guard officers arrayed chariots and horsemen and unfurled banners and standards.
translations.idiomatic: At Han court assemblies, guard officers deployed chariots and cavalry and raised banners and standards.

sentences.zh: 唐沿隋制，置衛尉卿，掌儀仗帳幕之事。

translations.literal: The Tang followed the Sui system and established the Director of the Imperial Guard, who oversaw ceremonial regalia and canopy affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang adopted the Sui arrangement, appointing a Director of the Imperial Guard to manage ceremonial equipment and ceremonial canopies.

sentences.zh: 宋衛 尉領左右金吾衛司、左右金吾仗司、六軍儀仗司，主清道、徼巡、排列、奉引儀 仗。

translations.literal: Under the Song, the Imperial Guard Directorate oversaw the Left and Right Golden Crow Guard Offices, the Left and Right Golden Crow Ceremonial Offices, and the Six Armies Ceremonial Office, charged with road clearing, patrol, formation, and presentation of ceremonial regalia.
translations.idiomatic: In Song times the Imperial Guard Directorate supervised the Left and Right Golden Crow guard offices, their ceremonial branches, and the Six Armies Ceremonial Office, responsible for clearing the way, patrol, marshaling formations, and leading the ceremonial train.

sentences.zh: 元置拱衛司，領控鶴戶以供其事。

translations.literal: The Yuan established the Imperial Escort Directorate, which oversaw Crane-Control households to supply its duties.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan created the Imperial Escort Directorate, drawing on Crane-Control households to perform these services.

sentences.zh: 歷代制度雖有沿革異同，總以謹出入之防， 嚴尊卑之分。

translations.literal: Although institutions changed through the dynasties, in general they strictly guarded access and strictly distinguished superior from inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Institutions varied from dynasty to dynasty, yet all aimed to guard ingress and egress and to enforce the hierarchy of rank.

sentences.zh: 慎重則尊嚴，尊嚴則整肅，是故文謂之儀，武謂之衛。

translations.literal: When cautious and weighty, there is dignity; when dignified, there is order—hence the civil aspect is called ceremony and the martial aspect is called guard.
translations.idiomatic: Careful observance yields dignity, and dignity yields discipline; the civil aspect is therefore called ceremony and the martial aspect guard.

sentences.zh: 天子出，車 駕次第謂之鹵簿。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven went forth, the ordered sequence of his carriage escort was called the guard of honor.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went abroad, the ordered procession of his carriage escort was termed the guard of honor.

sentences.zh: 而唐制四品以上皆給鹵簿，則君臣並得通稱也。

translations.literal: Yet under Tang regulations all officials of the fourth rank and above were granted a guard of honor, so the term could be used alike for ruler and subject.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang rules, however, officials of the fourth rank and above also received a guard of honor, so ruler and subject alike could use the term.

sentences.zh: 明初詔禮官， 鹵簿彌文，務從省節，以示尚質去奢之意。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Ming an edict ordered the ritual officials that the guard of honor had grown overly elaborate and should be simplified to show esteem for simplicity and rejection of extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty the emperor instructed the ritual officials to pare back the guard of honor, keeping it spare to signal a preference for plainness over luxury.

sentences.zh: 凡正、至、聖節、朝會，及冊拜、接 見蕃臣，儀鸞司陳設儀仗。

translations.literal: For the first day of the year, the winter solstice, sacred festivals, court assemblies, investiture audiences, and receptions of foreign tributaries, the Ceremonial Phoenix Office set out ceremonial regalia.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day, the winter solstice, imperial birthdays, court assemblies, investiture ceremonies, and audiences with foreign envoys, the Ceremonial Phoenix Office deployed the ceremonial train.

sentences.zh: 而中宮、東宮、親王皆有儀仗之制。

translations.literal: The empress, the heir apparent, and imperial princes each had their own regulations for ceremonial regalia.
translations.idiomatic: The empress, the heir apparent, and imperial princes each had prescribed ceremonial trains as well.

sentences.zh: 後或隨時增飾， 要以洪武創制爲準則焉。

translations.literal: Later additions were made from time to time, but the Hongwu founding regulations remained the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Later reigns sometimes added embellishments, yet the Hongwu founding code remained the touchstone.

sentences.zh: 茲撮《集禮》所載大凡，以備考覈。

translations.literal: Here the main points recorded in the Collected Rites are excerpted for reference and verification.
translations.idiomatic: What follows excerpts the principal entries in the Collected Rites for reference and verification.

sentences.zh: 其郡王及皇妃、東 宮妃以下儀仗，載在《會典》者，並著於篇云。

translations.literal: The ceremonial regalia of territorial princes, imperial consorts, and consorts of the heir apparent and below, as recorded in the Statutes, are also set down in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial trains of territorial princes, imperial consorts, and consorts of the heir apparent and below, as recorded in the Statutes, are likewise included here.

sentences.zh: 皇帝儀仗：吳元年十二月辛酉，中書左相國李善長率禮官以即位禮儀進。

translations.literal: The emperor's ceremonial regalia: On the xinyou day of the twelfth month of the first year of Wu, Left Chancellor of the Secretariat Li Shanchang led the ritual officials in presenting the enthronement ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's ceremonial train: On the xinyou day of the twelfth month of the first Wu year, Left Chancellor Li Shanchang led the ritual officials in presenting the enthronement rites.

sentences.zh: 是 日清晨，拱衛司陳設鹵簿，列甲士於午門外之東西，列旗仗於奉天門外之東西。

translations.literal: That morning at dawn the Imperial Escort Directorate set out the guard of honor, lining armored soldiers east and west outside the Meridian Gate and arraying banners and regalia east and west outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn that day the Imperial Escort Directorate arrayed the guard of honor, posting armored soldiers to the east and west of the Meridian Gate and ceremonial banners to the east and west of the Gate of Supreme Harmony.

sentences.zh: 龍旗十二，分左右，用甲士十二人。

translations.literal: Twelve dragon banners, divided left and right, with twelve armored soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve dragon banners, six to each side, borne by twelve armored soldiers.

sentences.zh: 北斗旗一、纛一居前，豹尾一居後，俱用甲 士三人。

translations.literal: One Big Dipper banner and one great banner went before, one leopard-tail standard behind, each with three armored soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: One Big Dipper banner and one command banner led the way; one leopard-tail standard brought up the rear—three armored soldiers for each.

sentences.zh: 虎豹各二，馴象六，分左右。

translations.literal: Two each of tiger and leopard figures, six trained elephants, divided left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Two tiger and two leopard figures apiece, with six trained elephants, arrayed to left and right.

sentences.zh: 布旗六十四：門旗、日旗、月旗，青龍、 白虎、風、雲、雷、雨、江、河、淮、濟旗，天馬、天祿、白澤、朱雀、玄武等 旗，木、火、土、金、水五星旗，五嶽旗，熊旗，鸞旗及二十八宿旗，各六行；

translations.literal: Sixty-four cloth banners: gate, sun, and moon banners; Azure Dragon, White Tiger, wind, cloud, thunder, rain, Yangtze, Yellow River, Huai, and Ji banners; Heavenly Horse, Heavenly Blessing, White Marsh, Vermilion Bird, Dark Warrior, and other banners; Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, and Water Five Stars banners; Five Sacred Peaks banners; bear and phoenix banners; and the Twenty-eight Lunar Mansions banners, six rows each.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty-four cloth banners in all—gate, sun, and moon; Azure Dragon and White Tiger; wind, cloud, thunder, and rain; the Yangtze, Yellow River, Huai, and Ji; Heavenly Horse, Heavenly Blessing, White Marsh, Vermilion Bird, and Dark Warrior; the banners of the five elements and five sacred peaks; bear and phoenix; and the twenty-eight lunar mansions—each arrayed in six rows.

sentences.zh: 每旗用甲士五人，一人執旗，四人執弓弩。

translations.literal: Each banner employed five armored soldiers: one bore the banner, four bore bows and crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: Each banner was manned by five armored soldiers—one to carry it, four with bows and crossbows.

sentences.zh: 設五輅於奉天門外：玉輅居中，左金 輅，次革輅，右象輅，次木輅，俱並列。

translations.literal: Five imperial carriages were set outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony: the jade carriage in the center; to the left the gold carriage, then the leather carriage; to the right the ivory carriage, then the wood carriage—all ranged in parallel.
translations.idiomatic: Five imperial carriages stood outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony: the jade carriage at center; to its left the gold carriage and then the leather carriage; to its right the ivory carriage and then the wood carriage—all aligned abreast.

sentences.zh: 丹墀左右布黃麾仗、黃蓋、華蓋、曲蓋、 紫方傘、紅方傘、雉扇、朱團扇、羽葆幢、豹尾、龍頭竿、信幡、傳教幡、告止 幡、絳引幡、戟氅、戈氅、儀鍠氅等，各三行。

translations.literal: To left and right of the red courtyard were arrayed yellow command regalia, yellow canopies, flowered canopies, curved canopies, purple square umbrellas, red square umbrellas, pheasant-tail fans, vermilion round fans, feathered canopy staffs, leopard-tail standards, dragon-head poles, trust banners, instruction banners, stop banners, crimson guide banners, halberd pennants, dagger-axe pennants, ceremonial bell pennants, and the like, three rows each.
translations.idiomatic: On either side of the red courtyard stood yellow command regalia, yellow and flowered canopies, curved canopies, purple and red square umbrellas, pheasant-tail and vermilion round fans, feathered canopy staffs, leopard-tail and dragon-head poles, trust, instruction, stop, and crimson guide banners, and halberd, dagger-axe, and ceremonial bell pennants—three rows apiece.

sentences.zh: 丹陛左右陳幢節、響節、金節、 燭籠、青龍白虎幢、班劍、吾杖、立瓜、臥瓜、儀刀、鐙杖、戟、骨朵、朱雀玄 武幢等，各三行。

translations.literal: To left and right of the red steps were displayed canopy staffs, sounding staffs, gold staffs, candle lanterns, Azure Dragon and White Tiger canopy staffs, court swords, ceremonial staffs, standing melons, reclining melons, ceremonial blades, stirrup staffs, halberds, maces, Vermilion Bird and Dark Warrior canopy staffs, and the like, three rows each.
translations.idiomatic: Flanking the red steps were canopy staffs, sounding and gold staffs, candle lanterns, Azure Dragon and White Tiger canopy staffs, court swords, ceremonial staffs, standing and reclining melons, ceremonial blades, stirrup staffs, halberds, maces, and Vermilion Bird and Dark Warrior canopy staffs—again three rows each.

sentences.zh: 殿門左右設圓蓋一、金交椅、金腳踏、水盆、水罐、團黃扇、 紅扇。

translations.literal: To left and right of the hall doors were set one round canopy each, a gold folding chair, gold footrests, water basins, water jars, round yellow fans, and red fans.
translations.idiomatic: Beside the hall doors stood a round canopy on each side, a gold folding chair, gold footrests, basins and jars for water, round yellow fans, and red fans.

sentences.zh: 皆校尉擎執。

translations.literal: All were borne by guard commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Guard commandants bore them all.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年十月，定元旦朝賀儀：金吾衛於奉天門外分設旗幟。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Hongwu the New Year's Day congratulatory audience was fixed: the Golden Crow Guard set out banners outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Hongwu's first year the New Year's congratulatory audience was codified: the Golden Crow Guard posted banners outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony.

sentences.zh: 宿衛於午門外 分設兵仗。

translations.literal: The Palace Guard set out weapons outside the Meridian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Guard deployed arms outside the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 衛尉寺於奉天殿門及丹陛、丹墀設黃麾仗。

translations.literal: The Imperial Guard Office set yellow command regalia at the doors of the Hall of Supreme Harmony and on the red steps and courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Guard Office arrayed yellow command regalia at the hall doors, on the red steps, and in the red courtyard.

sentences.zh: 內使監擎執於殿上。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Palace Attendants bore items inside the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants bore regalia inside the hall.

sentences.zh: 凡遇 冬至、聖節、冊拜、親王及蕃使來朝，儀俱同。

translations.literal: Whenever the winter solstice, sacred festivals, investiture audiences, visits of imperial princes, or audiences with foreign envoys occurred, the ceremonies were the same.
translations.idiomatic: The winter solstice, imperial birthdays, investitures, visits by imperial princes, and audiences with foreign envoys all followed the same arrangement.

sentences.zh: 其宣詔赦、降香，則惟設奉天殿 門及丹陛儀仗、殿上擎執云。

translations.literal: For proclamation of amnesties and descent of incense, only regalia at the hall doors and red steps and items borne inside the hall were set out.
translations.idiomatic: For amnesty proclamations and incense offerings, only the hall-door and red-step regalia and items borne within the hall were deployed.

sentences.zh: 其陳布次第，午門外，刀、盾、殳、叉各置於東西， 甲士用赤。

translations.literal: The order of arrangement: outside the Meridian Gate, sabers, shields, spears, and forks were placed east and west, with armored soldiers in red.
translations.idiomatic: The disposition ran thus: outside the Meridian Gate, sabers, shields, spears, and forks stood east and west, manned by soldiers in red armor.

sentences.zh: 奉天門外中道，金吾、宿衛二衛設龍旗十二，分左右，用青甲士十二 人。

translations.literal: On the central way outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony, the Golden Crow and Palace Guards set twelve dragon banners, left and right, with twelve soldiers in green armor.
translations.idiomatic: Along the central avenue outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony, the Golden Crow and Palace Guards posted twelve dragon banners, six to a side, borne by twelve soldiers in green armor.

sentences.zh: 北斗旗一、纛一居前，豹尾一居後，俱用黑甲士三人。

translations.literal: One Big Dipper banner and one great banner went before, one leopard-tail standard behind, each with three soldiers in black armor.
translations.idiomatic: One Big Dipper banner and one command banner led; one leopard-tail standard followed—three soldiers in black armor for each.

sentences.zh: 虎豹各二，馴象六， 分左右。

translations.literal: Two each of tiger and leopard figures, six trained elephants, divided left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Two tiger and two leopard figures apiece and six trained elephants were posted to left and right.

sentences.zh: 左右布旗六十四：左前第一行，門旗二，每旗用紅甲士五人，內一人執 旗，旗下四人執弓箭。

translations.literal: Sixty-four cloth banners left and right: on the left front, first row, two gate banners, each with five soldiers in red armor, one bearing the banner and four below with bows and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty-four cloth banners to left and right: on the left front, first row, two gate banners, each with five soldiers in red armor—one bearing the banner, four beneath with bows and arrows.

sentences.zh: 第二行，月旗一，用白甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人 執弩；

translations.literal: Second row, one moon banner, with five soldiers in white armor, one bearing the banner and four below with crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: Second row: one moon banner with five soldiers in white armor—one bearing it, four beneath with crossbows.

sentences.zh: 青龍旗一，用青甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弩。

translations.literal: One Azure Dragon banner, with five soldiers in green armor, one bearing the banner and four below with crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: One Azure Dragon banner with five soldiers in green armor—one bearing it, four beneath with crossbows.

sentences.zh: 第三行，風、雲、 雷、雨旗各一，每旗用黑甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弓箭；

translations.literal: Third row, one each of wind, cloud, thunder, and rain banners, each with five soldiers in black armor, one bearing the banner and four below with bows and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Third row: one wind, cloud, thunder, and rain banner apiece, each with five soldiers in black armor—one bearing the banner, four beneath with bows and arrows.

sentences.zh: 天馬、白澤、 朱雀旗各一，每旗用紅甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弓箭。

translations.literal: One each of Heavenly Horse, White Marsh, and Vermilion Bird banners, each with five soldiers in red armor, one bearing the banner and four below with bows and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: One Heavenly Horse, White Marsh, and Vermilion Bird banner apiece, each with five soldiers in red armor—one bearing the banner, four beneath with bows and arrows.

sentences.zh: 第四行，木、 火、土、金、水五星旗各一，隨其方色，每旗用甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四 人執弩，其甲木青、火紅、土黃、金白、水黑、熊旗、鸞旗各一，每旗用紅甲士 五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弩。

translations.literal: Fourth row, one each of Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, and Water Five Stars banners, in their directional colors, each with five armored soldiers, one bearing the banner and four below with crossbows—their armor being green for Wood, red for Fire, yellow for Earth, white for Metal, black for Water; one bear banner and one phoenix banner, each with five soldiers in red armor, one bearing the banner and four below with crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth row: one banner each for Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, and Water, colored to their directions, each with five armored soldiers—one bearing the banner, four beneath with crossbows—armor green for Wood, red for Fire, yellow for Earth, white for Metal, black for Water; plus one bear and one phoenix banner, each with five soldiers in red armor.

sentences.zh: 第五行角、亢、氐、房、心、尾、箕旗各一， 每旗用青甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弓箭。

translations.literal: Fifth row, one each of Horn, Neck, Root, Room, Heart, Tail, and Winnowing Basket banners, each with five soldiers in green armor, one bearing the banner and four below with bows and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth row: one banner each for Horn, Neck, Root, Room, Heart, Tail, and Winnowing Basket, each with five soldiers in green armor—one bearing the banner, four beneath with bows and arrows.

sentences.zh: 第六行鬥、牛、女、虛、危、 室、壁旗各一，每旗用青甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弩。

translations.literal: Sixth row, one each of Dipper, Ox, Girl, Void, Rooftop, Encampment, and Wall banners, each with five soldiers in green armor, one bearing the banner and four below with crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth row: one banner each for Dipper, Ox, Girl, Void, Rooftop, Encampment, and Wall, each with five soldiers in green armor—one bearing the banner, four beneath with crossbows.

sentences.zh: 右前第一行， 門旗二，每旗用紅甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弓箭。

translations.literal: On the right front, first row, two gate banners, each with five soldiers in red armor, one bearing the banner and four below with bows and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: On the right front, first row: two gate banners, each with five soldiers in red armor—one bearing the banner, four beneath with bows and arrows.

sentences.zh: 第二行，日旗一， 用紅甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弩；

translations.literal: Second row, one sun banner, with five soldiers in red armor, one bearing the banner and four below with crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: Second row: one sun banner with five soldiers in red armor—one bearing it, four beneath with crossbows.

sentences.zh: 白虎旗一，用白甲士五人，內一人 執旗，旗下四人執弩。

translations.literal: One White Tiger banner, with five soldiers in white armor, one bearing the banner and four below with crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: One White Tiger banner with five soldiers in white armor—one bearing it, four beneath with crossbows.

sentences.zh: 第三行，江、河、淮、濟旗各一，隨其方色，每旗用甲士 五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弓箭，其甲江紅、河白、淮青、濟黑；

translations.literal: Third row, one each of Yangtze, Yellow River, Huai, and Ji banners, in their directional colors, each with five armored soldiers, one bearing the banner and four below with bows and arrows—their armor being red for the Yangtze, white for the Yellow River, green for the Huai, black for the Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Third row: one Yangtze, Yellow River, Huai, and Ji banner apiece, each with five armored soldiers—armor red for the Yangtze, white for the Yellow River, green for the Huai, black for the Ji.

sentences.zh: 天祿、白 澤、玄武旗各一，每旗用甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弓箭，天祿、白澤 紅甲，玄武黑甲。

translations.literal: One each of Heavenly Blessing, White Marsh, and Dark Warrior banners, each with five armored soldiers, one bearing the banner and four below with bows and arrows—Heavenly Blessing and White Marsh in red armor, Dark Warrior in black armor.
translations.idiomatic: One Heavenly Blessing, White Marsh, and Dark Warrior banner apiece, each with five armored soldiers—Heavenly Blessing and White Marsh in red armor, Dark Warrior in black.

sentences.zh: 第四行，東、南、中、西、北五嶽旗各一，隨其方色，每旗用 甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弩，其甲東嶽青、南嶽紅、中嶽黃、西嶽白、 北嶽黑；

translations.literal: Fourth row, one each of the eastern, southern, central, western, and northern Five Sacred Peaks banners, in their directional colors, each with five armored soldiers, one bearing the banner and four below with crossbows—their armor being green for the eastern peak, red for the southern, yellow for the central, white for the western, black for the northern.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth row: one banner each for the eastern, southern, central, western, and northern sacred peaks, each with five armored soldiers—armor green, red, yellow, white, and black respectively.

sentences.zh: 熊旗、麟旗各一，每旗用紅甲士五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弩。

translations.literal: One bear banner and one qilin banner, each with five soldiers in red armor, one bearing the banner and four below with crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: One bear and one qilin banner, each with five soldiers in red armor—one bearing the banner, four beneath with crossbows.

sentences.zh: 第 五行，奎、婁、胃、昴、畢、觜、參旗各一，每旗用青甲士五人，內一人執旗， 旗下四人執弓箭。

translations.literal: Fifth row, one each of Striding Legs, Bond, Stomach, Hairy Head, Net, Turtle Beak, and Three Stars banners, each with five soldiers in green armor, one bearing the banner and four below with bows and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth row: one banner each for Striding Legs, Bond, Stomach, Hairy Head, Net, Turtle Beak, and Three Stars, each with five soldiers in green armor.

sentences.zh: 第六行，井、鬼、柳、星、張、翼、軫旗各一，每旗用青甲士 五人，內一人執旗，旗下四人執弩。

translations.literal: Sixth row, one each of Well, Ghost, Willow, Star, Extended Net, Wings, and Chariot banners, each with five soldiers in green armor, one bearing the banner and four below with crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth row: one banner each for Well, Ghost, Willow, Star, Extended Net, Wings, and Chariot, each with five soldiers in green armor—one bearing the banner, four beneath with crossbows.

sentences.zh: 奉天門外，拱衛司設五輅。

translations.literal: Outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony, the Imperial Escort Directorate set the five imperial carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the Gate of Supreme Harmony the Imperial Escort Directorate arrayed the five imperial carriages.

sentences.zh: 玉輅居中；

translations.literal: The jade carriage in the center.
translations.idiomatic: The jade carriage at center.

sentences.zh: 左金 輅，次革輅；

translations.literal: To the left the gold carriage, then the leather carriage.
translations.idiomatic: To its left the gold carriage, then the leather carriage.

sentences.zh: 右象輅，次木輅。

translations.literal: To the right the ivory carriage, then the wood carriage.
translations.idiomatic: To its right the ivory carriage, then the wood carriage.

sentences.zh: 俱並列。

translations.literal: All ranged in parallel.
translations.idiomatic: All aligned abreast.

sentences.zh: 典牧所設乘馬於文武樓之南，各三，東 西相向。

translations.literal: The Pasturage Office set riding horses south of the Civil and Military Tower, three each, facing east and west.
translations.idiomatic: The Pasturage Office posted riding horses south of the Civil and Military Tower, three on each side, facing one another east and west.

sentences.zh: 丹墀左右布黃麾仗凡九十，分左右，各三行。

translations.literal: To left and right of the red courtyard were arrayed ninety pieces of yellow command regalia, divided left and right, three rows each.
translations.idiomatic: Ninety pieces of yellow command regalia lined the red courtyard to left and right, three rows on each side.

sentences.zh: 左前第一行，十五：黃蓋 一，紅大傘二，華蓋一，曲蓋一，紫方傘一，紅方傘一，雉扇四，朱團扇四。

translations.literal: Left front, first row, fifteen items: one yellow canopy, two large red umbrellas, one flowered canopy, one curved canopy, one purple square umbrella, one red square umbrella, four pheasant-tail fans, four vermilion round fans.
translations.idiomatic: Left front, first row—fifteen items: one yellow canopy, two large red umbrellas, one flowered and one curved canopy, one purple and one red square umbrella, four pheasant-tail fans, and four vermilion round fans.

sentences.zh: 第 二行，十五：羽葆幢二，豹尾二，龍頭竿二，信幡二，傳教幡二，告止幡二，絳 引幡二，黃麾一。

translations.literal: Second row, fifteen: two feathered canopy staffs, two leopard-tail standards, two dragon-head poles, two trust banners, two instruction banners, two stop banners, two crimson guide banners, one yellow command staff.
translations.idiomatic: Second row—fifteen: two feathered canopy staffs, two leopard-tail standards, two dragon-head poles, two each of trust, instruction, stop, and crimson guide banners, and one yellow command staff.

sentences.zh: 第三行，十五：戟氅五，戈氅五，儀鍠氅五。

translations.literal: Third row, fifteen: five halberd pennants, five dagger-axe pennants, five ceremonial bell pennants.
translations.idiomatic: Third row—fifteen: five halberd pennants, five dagger-axe pennants, and five ceremonial bell pennants.

sentences.zh: 右前第一行，十 五：黃蓋一，紅大傘二，華蓋一，曲蓋一，紫方傘一，紅方傘一，雉扇四，朱團 扇四。

translations.literal: Right front, first row, fifteen: one yellow canopy, two large red umbrellas, one flowered canopy, one curved canopy, one purple square umbrella, one red square umbrella, four pheasant-tail fans, four vermilion round fans.
translations.idiomatic: Right front, first row—fifteen: the same array as on the left.

sentences.zh: 第二行，十五：羽葆幢二，豹尾二，龍頭竿二，信幡二，傳教幡二，告止 幡二，絳引幡二，黃麾一。

translations.literal: Second row, fifteen: two feathered canopy staffs, two leopard-tail standards, two dragon-head poles, two trust banners, two instruction banners, two stop banners, two crimson guide banners, one yellow command staff.
translations.idiomatic: Second row—fifteen: matching the left side in every item.

sentences.zh: 第三行，十五：戟氅五，戈氅五，儀鍠氅五。

translations.literal: Third row, fifteen: five halberd pennants, five dagger-axe pennants, five ceremonial bell pennants.
translations.idiomatic: Third row—fifteen: five halberd pennants, five dagger-axe pennants, and five ceremonial bell pennants.

sentences.zh: 皆校尉 擎執。

translations.literal: All were borne by guard commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Guard commandants bore them all.

sentences.zh: 丹陛左右，拱衛司陳幢節等仗九十，分左右，爲四行。

translations.literal: To left and right of the red steps, the Imperial Escort Directorate displayed ninety canopy staffs and other regalia, divided left and right into four rows.
translations.idiomatic: Flanking the red steps, the Imperial Escort Directorate arrayed ninety canopy staffs and allied regalia in four rows to each side.

sentences.zh: 左前第一行，響節 十二，金節三，燭籠三。

translations.literal: Left front, first row: twelve sounding staffs, three gold staffs, three candle lanterns.
translations.idiomatic: Left front, first row: twelve sounding staffs, three gold staffs, and three candle lanterns.

sentences.zh: 第二行，青龍幢一，班劍三，吾杖三，立瓜三，臥瓜三， 儀刀三，鐙杖三，戟三，骨朵三，朱雀幢一。

translations.literal: Second row: one Azure Dragon canopy staff, three court swords, three ceremonial staffs, three standing melons, three reclining melons, three ceremonial blades, three stirrup staffs, three halberds, three maces, one Vermilion Bird canopy staff.
translations.idiomatic: Second row: one Azure Dragon canopy staff, three each of court swords, ceremonial staffs, standing and reclining melons, ceremonial blades, stirrup staffs, halberds, and maces, and one Vermilion Bird canopy staff.

sentences.zh: 右前第一行，響節十二，金節三， 燭籠三。

translations.literal: Right front, first row: twelve sounding staffs, three gold staffs, three candle lanterns.
translations.idiomatic: Right front, first row: twelve sounding staffs, three gold staffs, and three candle lanterns.

sentences.zh: 第二行，白虎幢一，班劍三，吾杖三，立瓜三，臥瓜三，儀刀三，鐙杖 三，戟三，骨朵三，玄武幢一。

translations.literal: Second row: one White Tiger canopy staff, three court swords, three ceremonial staffs, three standing melons, three reclining melons, three ceremonial blades, three stirrup staffs, three halberds, three maces, one Dark Warrior canopy staff.
translations.idiomatic: Second row: one White Tiger canopy staff, three each of the same weapons and regalia as on the left, and one Dark Warrior canopy staff.

sentences.zh: 皆校尉擎執。

translations.literal: All were borne by guard commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Guard commandants bore them all.

sentences.zh: 奉天殿門左右，拱衛司陳設：左行， 圓蓋一，金腳踏一，金水盆一，團黃扇三，紅扇三；

translations.literal: To left and right of the doors of the Hall of Supreme Harmony, the Imperial Escort Directorate set out: on the left, one round canopy, one gold footrest, one gold water basin, three round yellow fans, three red fans.
translations.idiomatic: Beside the doors of the Hall of Supreme Harmony the Imperial Escort Directorate posted: on the left, one round canopy, one gold footrest, one gold water basin, three round yellow fans, and three red fans.

sentences.zh: 右行，圓蓋一，金交椅一， 金水罐一，團黃扇三，紅扇三。

translations.literal: On the right, one round canopy, one gold folding chair, one gold water jar, three round yellow fans, three red fans.
translations.idiomatic: On the right, one round canopy, one gold folding chair, one gold water jar, three round yellow fans, and three red fans.

sentences.zh: 皆校尉擎執。

translations.literal: All were borne by guard commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Guard commandants bore them all.

sentences.zh: 殿上左右內使監陳設：左，拂子二， 金唾壺一，金香合一；

translations.literal: Inside the hall, left and right, the Directorate of Palace Attendants set out: on the left, two whisk fans, one gold spittoon, one gold incense box.
translations.idiomatic: Within the hall the palace attendants arranged: on the left, two whisk fans, one gold spittoon, and one gold incense box.

sentences.zh: 右，拂子二，金唾盂一，金香爐一。

translations.literal: On the right, two whisk fans, one gold spittoon bowl, one gold incense burner.
translations.idiomatic: On the right, two whisk fans, one gold spittoon bowl, and one gold incense burner.

sentences.zh: 皆內使擎執。

translations.literal: All were borne by palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants bore them all.

sentences.zh: 和聲郎 陳樂於丹墀文武官拜位之南，其器數詳見《樂志》內。

translations.literal: Harmony Officers set out music south of the civil and military officials' obeisance positions on the red courtyard; the number of instruments is detailed in the Treatise on Music.
translations.idiomatic: Harmony Officers stationed musicians south of the civil and military officials' obeisance marks on the red courtyard; instrument counts appear in the Treatise on Music.

sentences.zh: 三年，命制郊丘祭祀拜褥。

translations.literal: In the third year an order was issued to make kneeling mats for suburban altar sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the court ordered kneeling mats made for suburban altar rites.

sentences.zh: 郊丘用席表蒲裏爲褥，宗廟、社稷、先農、山川 用紅文綺表紅木棉布裏爲褥。

translations.literal: For suburban altars, mats with rush matting on the outside and rush padding within were used; for the ancestral temple, altars of soil and grain, the god of agriculture, and mountains and rivers, mats with red patterned silk on the outside and red wood-cotton cloth within were used.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban altars used mats faced with rush matting and padded with rush; the ancestral temple, altars of soil and grain, the god of agriculture, and mountain-and-river sacrifices used mats faced with red patterned silk and lined with red cotton cloth.

sentences.zh: 十二年，命禮部增設丹墀儀仗，黃傘、華蓋、曲蓋、 紫方傘、紅方傘各二，雉扇、紅團扇各四，羽葆幢、龍頭竿、絳引、傳教、告止、 信幡各六，戟氅、戈氅、儀鍠氅各十。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Ministry of Rites was ordered to add ceremonial regalia on the red courtyard: two each of yellow umbrellas, flowered canopies, curved canopies, purple square umbrellas, and red square umbrellas; four each of pheasant-tail fans and red round fans; six each of feathered canopy staffs, dragon-head poles, crimson guide, instruction, stop, and trust banners; ten each of halberd, dagger-axe, and ceremonial bell pennants.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the Ministry of Rites was told to expand red-courtyard regalia: two each of yellow, flowered, and curved canopies and purple and red square umbrellas; four pheasant-tail and red round fans apiece; six each of feathered canopy staffs, dragon-head poles, and crimson guide, instruction, stop, and trust banners; and ten each of halberd, dagger-axe, and ceremonial bell pennants.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，禮部言鹵簿中宜有九龍車一乘，請增置。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle the Ministry of Rites said the guard of honor ought to include one Nine Dragons carriage and requested that it be added.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle's first year the Ministry of Rites proposed adding a Nine Dragons carriage to the guard of honor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「禮貴得中，過 爲奢，不及爲儉，先朝審之精矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Rites value hitting the mean; excess is extravagance, shortfall is austerity—the previous dynasty judged this with precision."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Ritual prizes the mean; excess is luxury and shortfall is stinginess—and the founding court weighed that with care."

sentences.zh: 當遵用舊章，豈可輒有增益，以啓後世之奢哉？

translations.literal: "The old regulations should be followed—how could additions be made lightly and open the way to extravagance for later ages?"
translations.idiomatic: "We should keep to the old code. How could we add to it lightly and teach later generations to be lavish?"

sentences.zh: 九龍車既先朝所無，其仍舊便。

translations.literal: "Since the Nine Dragons carriage did not exist in the previous dynasty, let things remain as they are."
translations.idiomatic: "The Nine Dragons carriage never existed under the founders—leave matters as they are."

sentences.zh: 」宣德元年，更造鹵簿儀仗，有具服幄殿一座， 金交椅一，金腳踏一，金盆一，金罐一，金馬杌一，鞍籠一，金香爐一，金香合 一，金唾盂一，金唾壺一，御杖二，擺錫明甲一百副，盔一百，弓一百，箭三千， 刀一百。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuande the guard of honor regalia was remade, including one full-dress tent-palace, one gold folding chair, one gold footrest, one gold basin, one gold jar, one gold horse stool, one saddle case, one gold incense burner, one gold incense box, one gold spittoon bowl, one gold spittoon pot, two imperial staffs, one hundred sets of bright tin armor displayed, one hundred helmets, one hundred bows, three thousand arrows, one hundred sabers.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande's first year the guard-of-honor regalia was remade: a full-dress tent-palace; one gold folding chair, footrest, basin, and jar; one gold horse stool and saddle case; gold incense burner and box; gold spittoon bowl and pot; two imperial staffs; and one hundred sets of bright tin armor on display, with matching helmets, bows, three thousand arrows, and sabers.

sentences.zh: 其執事校尉，每人鵝帽，只孫衣，銅帶靴履鞋一副。

translations.literal: The guard commandants on duty each wore goose-down caps, single-layer grandson garments, copper belts, and one set each of boots, shoes, and sandals.
translations.idiomatic: Duty commandants each wore goose-down caps, single-layer grandson garments, copper belts, and full sets of boots and shoes.

sentences.zh: 常朝，各色羅掌扇 四十，各色羅絹傘十，萬壽傘一，黃雙龍扇二。

translations.literal: For regular audiences: forty palm fans of various colored silks, ten umbrellas of various colored silks, one Longevity umbrella, two yellow double-dragon fans.
translations.idiomatic: For regular audiences: forty palm fans in assorted colored silks, ten silk umbrellas, one Longevity umbrella, and two yellow double-dragon fans.

sentences.zh: 筵宴，銷金羅傘四，銷金雨傘四， 金龍響節二十四。

translations.literal: For banquets: four gold-brocaded silk umbrellas, four gold-brocaded rain umbrellas, twenty-four gold-dragon sounding staffs.
translations.idiomatic: For banquets: four gold-brocaded silk umbrellas, four gold-brocaded rain umbrellas, and twenty-four gold-dragon sounding staffs.

sentences.zh: 皇太子儀仗，洪武元年定：門外中道設龍旗六，其執龍旗者並戎服。

translations.literal: The crown prince's ceremonial regalia, fixed in the first year of Hongwu: six dragon banners were set on the central way outside the gate, and those bearing the dragon banners all wore military dress.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's ceremonial train, fixed in Hongwu's first year: six dragon banners on the central avenue outside the gate, all bearers in military dress.

sentences.zh: 黃旗一 居中，左前青旗一，右前赤旗一，左後黑旗一，右後白旗一，每旗執弓弩軍士六 人，服各隨旗色。

translations.literal: One yellow banner in the center; one green banner forward left, one red banner forward right, one black banner rear left, one white banner rear right; each banner had six soldiers with bows and crossbows, their dress matching the banner color.
translations.idiomatic: One yellow banner at center; green forward left, red forward right, black rear left, white rear right—six archers per banner, dressed to match its color.

sentences.zh: 殿下設三十六人：絳引幡二，戟氅六，戈氅六，儀鍠氅六，羽 葆幢六，青方傘二，青小方扇四，青雜花團扇四，皆校尉擎執。

translations.literal: Below the hall thirty-six men were set: two crimson guide banners, six halberd pennants, six dagger-axe pennants, six ceremonial bell pennants, six feathered canopy staffs, two green square umbrellas, four small green square fans, four green mixed-flower round fans—all borne by guard commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Below the hall stood thirty-six commandants bearing two crimson guide banners, six each of halberd, dagger-axe, and ceremonial bell pennants, six feathered canopy staffs, two green square umbrellas, four small green square fans, and four green floral round fans.

sentences.zh: 殿前設四十八人： 班劍四，吾杖四，立瓜四，臥瓜四，儀刀四，鐙杖四，骨朵四，斧四，響節十二， 金節四，皆校尉擎執。

translations.literal: Before the hall forty-eight men were set: four court swords, four ceremonial staffs, four standing melons, four reclining melons, four ceremonial blades, four stirrup staffs, four maces, four axes, twelve sounding staffs, four gold staffs—all borne by guard commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Before the hall stood forty-eight commandants with four each of court swords, ceremonial staffs, standing and reclining melons, ceremonial blades, stirrup staffs, maces, and axes, plus twelve sounding staffs and four gold staffs.

sentences.zh: 殿門設十二人：金交椅一，金腳踏一，金水罐一，金水盆 一，青羅團扇六，紅圓蓋二，皆校尉擎執。

translations.literal: At the hall doors twelve men were set: one gold folding chair, one gold footrest, one gold water jar, one gold water basin, six green silk round fans, two red round canopies—all borne by guard commandants.
translations.idiomatic: At the hall doors twelve commandants bore one gold folding chair, one gold footrest, one gold water jar and basin, six green silk round fans, and two red round canopies.

sentences.zh: 殿上設六人：金香爐一，香合一，唾 盂一，唾壺一，拂子二，皆內使擎執。

translations.literal: Inside the hall six men were set: one gold incense burner, one incense box, one spittoon bowl, one spittoon pot, two whisk fans—all borne by palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Within the hall six attendants bore one gold incense burner and box, one spittoon bowl and pot, and two whisk fans.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年，禮部言，東宮儀仗，有司失紀 載，視親王差少，宜增制金香爐、金香合各一，殳二，叉二，傳教、告止、信幡 各二，節二，幢二，夾槊二，槊、刀、盾各二十，戟八，紅紙油燈籠六，紅羅銷 金邊圓傘、紅羅繡圓傘各一，紅羅曲蓋繡傘、紅羅素圓傘、紅羅素方傘、青羅素 方傘各二，紅羅繡孔雀方扇、紅羅繡四季花團扇各四，拂子二，唾盂、唾壺各一， 鞍籠一，誕馬八，紅令旗二，清道旗四，幰弩一，白澤旗二，弓箭二十副。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle the Ministry of Rites said the Eastern Palace ceremonial regalia had not been fully recorded by the responsible offices and was somewhat less than that of imperial princes; it should be augmented with one each of gold incense burner and gold incense box, two spears, two forks, two each of instruction, stop, and trust banners, two staffs, two canopy staffs, two paired lances, twenty each of lances, sabers, and shields, eight halberds, six red-paper oil lanterns, one each of red silk gold-brocaded round umbrella and red silk embroidered round umbrella, two each of red silk curved embroidered umbrella, red silk plain round umbrella, red silk plain square umbrella, and green silk plain square umbrella, four each of red silk embroidered peacock square fans and red silk embroidered four-seasons-flower round fans, two whisk fans, one each of spittoon bowl and spittoon pot, one saddle case, eight presentation horses, two red command banners, four road-clearing banners, one covered crossbow carriage, two White Marsh banners, twenty sets of bow and arrow.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle's second year the Ministry of Rites reported that the heir apparent's ceremonial train had been under-recorded and fell short of a prince's equipage. They proposed adding gold incense burner and box; spears and forks; instruction, stop, and trust banners; staffs and canopy staffs; paired lances; twenty lances, sabers, and shields apiece; eight halberds; six red-paper oil lanterns; assorted red and green silk umbrellas and fans; whisk fans and spittoons; a saddle case; eight presentation horses; command and road-clearing banners; a covered crossbow carriage; two White Marsh banners; and twenty sets of bow and arrow.

sentences.zh: 從 之。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 親王儀仗，洪武六年定：宮門外設方色旗二，青色白澤旗二，執人服隨旗色， 並戎服。

translations.literal: Imperial princes' ceremonial regalia, fixed in the sixth year of Hongwu: outside the palace gate two directional-color banners and two green White Marsh banners were set; bearers dressed according to banner color, all in military dress.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes' ceremonial train, fixed in Hongwu's sixth year: outside the palace gate stood two directional-color banners and two green White Marsh banners, bearers in military dress colored to match.

sentences.zh: 殿下，絳引幡二，戟氅二，戈氅二，儀鍠氅二，皆校尉執。

translations.literal: Below the hall: two crimson guide banners, two halberd pennants, two dagger-axe pennants, two ceremonial bell pennants—all borne by guard commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Below the hall: two crimson guide banners and two each of halberd, dagger-axe, and ceremonial bell pennants, all borne by guard commandants.

sentences.zh: 殿前，班劍 二，吾杖二，立瓜二，臥瓜二，儀刀二，鐙杖二，骨朵二，斧二，響節八，皆校 尉執。

translations.literal: Before the hall: two court swords, two ceremonial staffs, two standing melons, two reclining melons, two ceremonial blades, two stirrup staffs, two maces, two axes, eight sounding staffs—all borne by guard commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Before the hall: two each of court swords, ceremonial staffs, standing and reclining melons, ceremonial blades, stirrup staffs, maces, and axes, plus eight sounding staffs—all borne by guard commandants.

sentences.zh: 殿門，交椅一，腳踏一，水罐一，水盆一，團扇四，蓋二，皆校尉執。

translations.literal: At the hall doors: one folding chair, one footrest, one water jar, one water basin, four round fans, two canopies—all borne by guard commandants.
translations.idiomatic: At the hall doors: one folding chair, footrest, water jar and basin, four round fans, and two canopies—all borne by guard commandants.

sentences.zh: 殿 上，拂子二，香爐一，香合一，唾壺一，唾盂一。

translations.literal: Inside the hall: two whisk fans, one incense burner, one incense box, one spittoon pot, one spittoon bowl.
translations.idiomatic: Within the hall: two whisk fans, one incense burner and box, and one spittoon pot and bowl.

sentences.zh: 十六年詔，親王儀仗內交椅、 盆、罐用銀者，悉改用金。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year an edict ordered that folding chairs, basins, and jars of silver in imperial princes' ceremonial regalia all be changed to gold.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year an edict required that silver folding chairs, basins, and jars in princes' ceremonial trains be replaced with gold.

sentences.zh: 建文四年，禮部言，親王儀仗合增紅油絹銷金雨傘一， 紅紗燈籠、紅油紙燈籠各四，敔燈二，大小銅角四。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwen the Ministry of Rites said imperial princes' ceremonial regalia should add one red-oil-silk gold-brocaded rain umbrella, four each of red gauze lanterns and red-oil-paper lanterns, two yi-lamps, and four large and small bronze horns.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwen's fourth year the Ministry of Rites proposed adding to princes' trains one red-oil-silk gold-brocaded rain umbrella, four red gauze and four red-oil-paper lanterns, two yi-lamps, and four bronze horns large and small.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年命工部，親 王儀仗內紅銷金傘，仍用寶珠龍文。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongle the Ministry of Works was ordered that red gold-brocaded umbrellas in imperial princes' ceremonial regalia should still use pearl-and-dragon designs.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle's third year the Works Ministry was told that princes' red gold-brocaded umbrellas should retain pearl-and-dragon ornament.

sentences.zh: 凡世子儀仗同。

translations.literal: The heir apparent's ceremonial regalia was the same in all respects.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent's ceremonial train followed the same rules.

sentences.zh: 郡王儀仗：令旗二，清道旗二，幰弩一，刀盾十六，弓箭十八副，絳引、 傳教、告止、信幡各二，吾杖、儀刀、立瓜、臥瓜、骨朵、斧各二，戟十六，槊 十六，麾一，幢一，節一，響節六，紅銷金圓傘一，紅圓傘一，紅曲柄傘二，紅 方傘二，青圓扇四，紅圓扇四，誕馬四，鞍籠一，馬杌一，拂子二，交椅一，腳 踏一，水盆一，水罐一，香爐一，紅紗燈籠二，敔燈二，帳房一座。

translations.literal: Territorial princes' ceremonial regalia: two command banners, two road-clearing banners, one covered crossbow carriage, sixteen sabers and shields, eighteen sets of bow and arrow, two each of crimson guide, instruction, stop, and trust banners, two each of ceremonial staffs, ceremonial blades, standing melons, reclining melons, maces, and axes, sixteen halberds, sixteen lances, one command staff, one canopy staff, one staff, six sounding staffs, one red gold-brocaded round umbrella, one red round umbrella, two red curved-handle umbrellas, two red square umbrellas, four green round fans, four red round fans, four presentation horses, one saddle case, one horse stool, two whisk fans, one folding chair, one footrest, one water basin, one water jar, one incense burner, two red gauze lanterns, two yi-lamps, one tent quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Territorial princes' ceremonial train comprised two command and two road-clearing banners; a covered crossbow carriage; sixteen sabers and shields; eighteen bow-and-arrow sets; paired crimson guide, instruction, stop, and trust banners; paired ceremonial staffs, blades, melons, maces, and axes; sixteen halberds and lances; command, canopy, and sounding staffs; assorted red and green umbrellas and fans; four presentation horses; saddle case and horse stool; whisk fans; folding chair, footrest, basin, and jar; incense burner; lanterns; yi-lamps; and a tent quarters.

sentences.zh: 皇妃儀仗：紅杖二，清道旗二，絳引幡二，戈氅、戟氅、儀鍠氅、吾杖、儀 刀、班劍、立瓜、臥瓜、鐙杖、骨朵、金鉞各二，響節四，青方傘四，紅繡圓傘 一，繡方扇四，紅花圓扇四，青繡圓扇四，交椅一，腳踏一，拂子二，水盆一， 水罐一，香爐一，香合一，唾盂一，唾壺一，紅紗燈籠四。

translations.literal: Imperial consorts' ceremonial regalia: two red staffs, two road-clearing banners, two crimson guide banners, two each of dagger-axe pennants, halberd pennants, ceremonial bell pennants, ceremonial staffs, ceremonial blades, court swords, standing melons, reclining melons, stirrup staffs, maces, and gold axes, four sounding staffs, four green square umbrellas, one red embroidered round umbrella, four embroidered square fans, four red floral round fans, four green embroidered round fans, one folding chair, one footrest, two whisk fans, one water basin, one water jar, one incense burner, one incense box, one spittoon bowl, one spittoon pot, four red gauze lanterns.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial consorts' ceremonial train included two red staffs and road-clearing banners; paired crimson guide banners and pennants; paired court swords, melons, blades, maces, and gold axes; four sounding staffs; green and red umbrellas and fans; folding chair and footrest; whisk fans; basin and jar; incense burner and box; spittoons; and four red gauze lanterns.

sentences.zh: 東宮妃儀仗：紅杖二，清道旗二，絳引幡二，儀鍠氅、戈氅、戟氅、吾杖、 儀刀、班劍、立瓜、臥瓜、鐙杖、骨朵、金鉞各二，響節四，青方傘二，紅素圓 傘二，紅繡圓傘一，紅繡方扇四，紅繡花圓扇四，青繡圓扇四，交椅一，腳踏一， 拂子二，水盆一，水罐一，香爐一，香合一，紅紗燈籠四。

translations.literal: Consorts of the heir apparent's ceremonial regalia: two red staffs, two road-clearing banners, two crimson guide banners, two each of ceremonial bell pennants, dagger-axe pennants, halberd pennants, ceremonial staffs, ceremonial blades, court swords, standing melons, reclining melons, stirrup staffs, maces, and gold axes, four sounding staffs, two green square umbrellas, two plain red round umbrellas, one red embroidered round umbrella, four red embroidered square fans, four red embroidered floral round fans, four green embroidered round fans, one folding chair, one footrest, two whisk fans, one water basin, one water jar, one incense burner, one incense box, four red gauze lanterns.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts of the heir apparent had a train matching princely consorts in most items, with green and red umbrellas and fans, court regalia in pairs, folding chair and footrest, whisk fans, basin and jar, incense burner and box, and four red gauze lanterns.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年，禮部言， 東宮妃儀仗如親王妃，惟香爐、香合如中宮，但亦不用金，其水盆、水罐皆用銀， 從之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle the Ministry of Rites said consorts of the heir apparent should have ceremonial regalia like princely consorts, except that incense burner and box should follow the empress's pattern but also without gold; water basins and jars should all be silver. The proposal was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle's second year the Ministry of Rites ruled that an heir apparent's consort should mirror a princely consort's train, while incense burner and box followed the empress's model—but without gold—and basins and jars were to be silver. The court approved.

sentences.zh: 親王妃儀仗：紅杖二，清道旗二，絳引幡二，戟氅、吾杖、儀刀、班劍、立 瓜、臥瓜、骨朵、鐙杖各二，響節四，青方傘二，紅彩畫雲鳳傘一，青孔雀圓扇 四，紅花扇四，交椅一，腳踏一，水盆一，水罐一，紅紗燈籠四，拂子二。

translations.literal: Princely consorts' ceremonial regalia: two red staffs, two road-clearing banners, two crimson guide banners, two each of halberd pennants, ceremonial staffs, ceremonial blades, court swords, standing melons, reclining melons, maces, and stirrup staffs, four sounding staffs, two green square umbrellas, one red cloud-and-phoenix painted umbrella, four green peacock round fans, four red floral fans, one folding chair, one footrest, one water basin, one water jar, four red gauze lanterns, two whisk fans.
translations.idiomatic: Princely consorts' ceremonial train included paired red staffs, road-clearing and crimson guide banners, halberd pennants and court regalia, four sounding staffs, green and red umbrellas and fans, folding chair and footrest, basin and jar, four red gauze lanterns, and two whisk fans.

sentences.zh: 公主、 世子妃儀仗俱同。

translations.literal: Imperial princesses and consorts of heirs apparent had the same ceremonial regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princesses and heirs' consorts followed the same rules.

sentences.zh: 郡王妃儀仗：紅杖二，清道旗二，絳引幡二，戟氅、吾杖、班劍、立瓜、骨 朵各二，響節二，青方傘二，紅圓傘一，青圓扇二，紅圓扇二，交椅一，腳踏一， 拂子二，紅紗燈籠二，水盆一，水罐一。

translations.literal: Territorial princes' consorts' ceremonial regalia: two red staffs, two road-clearing banners, two crimson guide banners, two each of halberd pennants, ceremonial staffs, court swords, standing melons, and maces, two sounding staffs, two green square umbrellas, one red round umbrella, two green round fans, two red round fans, one folding chair, one footrest, two whisk fans, two red gauze lanterns, one water basin, one water jar.
translations.idiomatic: Territorial princes' consorts carried a reduced train: paired staffs, banners, and pennants; two sounding staffs; green and red umbrellas and fans; folding chair, footrest, whisk fans, lanterns, basin, and jar.

sentences.zh: 郡主儀仗：紅杖二，清道旗二，班劍、吾杖、立瓜、骨朵各二，響節二，青 方傘一，紅圓傘一，青圓扇二，紅圓扇二，交椅一，腳踏一，水盆一，水罐一， 紅紗燈籠二，拂子二。

translations.literal: Territorial princesses' ceremonial regalia: two red staffs, two road-clearing banners, two each of court swords, ceremonial staffs, standing melons, and maces, two sounding staffs, one green square umbrella, one red round umbrella, two green round fans, two red round fans, one folding chair, one footrest, one water basin, one water jar, two red gauze lanterns, two whisk fans.
translations.idiomatic: Territorial princesses had a still smaller train: paired staffs and road-clearing banners; court swords, staffs, melons, and maces; sounding staffs; umbrellas and fans; chair, footrest, basin, jar, lanterns, and whisk fans.

sentences.zh: 舊例，郡王儀仗有交椅、馬杌，皆木質銀裹；

translations.literal: Under the old regulations, territorial princes' ceremonial regalia included folding chairs and horse stools, all of wood wrapped in silver.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly a territorial prince's train included folding chair and horse stool of wood sheathed in silver.

sentences.zh: 水盆、水罐及香爐、香合，皆 銀質抹金；

translations.literal: Water basins, water jars, incense burners, and incense boxes were all of silver with gold overlay.
translations.idiomatic: Basins, jars, incense burner, and incense box were silver gilt.

sentences.zh: 量折銀三百二十兩。

translations.literal: Calculated as a silver commutation of three hundred and twenty taels.
translations.idiomatic: Commuted to three hundred and twenty taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 郡王妃儀仗，有交椅等大器，量折銀一百六十兩。

translations.literal: Territorial princes' consorts' ceremonial regalia, with folding chairs and other large vessels, was calculated as a silver commutation of one hundred and sixty taels.
translations.idiomatic: A territorial prince's consort, with folding chair and other major pieces, received a commutation of one hundred and sixty taels.

sentences.zh: 餘皆自備充用。

translations.literal: All remaining items were to be supplied by the recipients themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else they furnished at their own expense.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十四年定，除親王及親王妃初封儀仗照例頒給外，其初封 郡王及郡王妃折銀等項，並停止。

translations.literal: Fixed in the forty-fourth year of Jiajing: except that imperial princes and princely consorts on first enfeoffment still received ceremonial regalia according to precedent, silver commutations for first-enfeoffment territorial princes and their consorts were altogether discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing's forty-fourth year the court ruled that only imperial princes and princely consorts on first enfeoffment would still receive full trains as before; silver commutations for newly enfeoffed territorial princes and their consorts were abolished.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十年定，郡王初封系帝孫者，儀仗照例全 給，系王孫者免。

translations.literal: Fixed in the tenth year of Wanli: territorial princes on first enfeoffment who were grandsons of the emperor received the full ceremonial regalia according to precedent; those who were grandsons of princes were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli's tenth year a compromise held: a territorial prince on first enfeoffment who was the emperor's grandson still received a full train, but a prince's grandson did not.

sentences.zh: 蓋宗室分封漸多，勢難遍給也。

translations.literal: This was because enfeoffments within the imperial clan grew ever more numerous, and it was difficult to supply all in full.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen multiplied with each generation, and the court could no longer outfit them all.
